column3: “In an instant, suddenly” preserves the double expression of suddenness.
Says “consecrate his head on that day,” without an explicit added “again.”
“The former days shall fall” preserves the image rendered “shall not be counted.”
The basket and its cakes precede the grain and drink offerings, rather than following them.
Repeats “the hair of the head of his consecration,” rather than reducing the second occurrence to “the hair.”
“What his hand can attain” preserves the hand image rendered “whatever else he can afford.”
